content.text:
This confirms it: commit 9431bdc995af7ff28a6a227dcf9e07f3f0135069 introduced the `isRTLCharacter` method from scratch, with the brand-new (and incorrect) upper bound `0xFEFF` for the `0xFE70` range. The fixing commit 8e0deafda38 simply corrects this single boundary to `0xFEFE`. There is no earlier version of this method or line to trace back further — this is the original introduction.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 9431bdc995af7ff28a6a227dcf9e07f3f0135069

## Reasoning
(1) I used `git log -p --follow` on `core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java` to trace the history of the modified line (`c <= 0xFEFF` / `0xFEFE`). This showed that the line with the incorrect value `0xFEFF` first appears in exactly one earlier commit before the fix.

(2) That commit, 9431bdc995af7ff28a6a227dcf9e07f3f0135069 (same author, Eran Mizrahi, two days earlier), adds the entirely new `isRTLCharacter(char c)` method (along with `hasRTLCharacters` and bidi-processing helpers) as part of a larger RTL/bidi reshaping feature. The method's final range check was written as `(c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)`, which is off-by-one: `0xFEFF` is the Unicode byte-order-mark / noncharacter, not part of the Arabic Presentation Forms-B RTL block (U+FE70–U+FEFE). This is precisely the character-range bug that commit 8e0deafda38 later fixes by changing `0xFEFF` to `0xFEFE`.

(3) Evidence: the `grep` on the full file history shows only two occurrences of this boundary constant in the entire project history — the introduction in 9431bdc99 and the one-character fix in 8e0deafda. There is no other commit touching this line in between, so 9431bdc99 is unambiguously the commit that introduced the off-by-one bug. Confidence is high.
